parsed.explanation: The combined regime is hostile at the border and in state-run facilities, but there is no general criminalisation of transgender identity and national hate-crime, employment and marriage protections exist. The decisive traveller exposures are national passport/entry screening — binary sex markers, refusal where documents or presentation cast doubt, and possible permanent fraud ineligibility — and state law permitting bathroom exclusion in many government facilities, with trespass enforcement documented elsewhere. No working remedy is documented for these exposures; the state lacks gender-identity hate-crime and anti-discrimination coverage. Detention and custody carry severe documented harms, but are conditional. Private hospitality is less restricted. A lone adult and an adult with a minor both face border and facility outing; the minor adds disclosure and facility risk. This is Elevated Risk, not Severe Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary sex definition; no new X markers; officers may refuse discrepant cases and consider permanent fraud ineligibility; passports reported confiscated or blocked, stranding travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; litigation is pending; fraud finding is not automatic and requires four elements.
entry_documents.interaction: Passport/presentation mismatch at border can trigger secondary screening, refusal or fraud inquiry; state birth-certificate closure increases disclosure when documents are examined.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of transgender men; corrections policies include conversion practices; a bathroom arrest occurred in another state.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some national orders are enjoined; no state gender-identity hate-crime protection.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border fraud suspicion can lead to immigration detention; a facility-access refusal can escalate to trespass arrest if the person refuses to leave.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State 2023 law permits restricting transgender bathroom use in many state-run facilities; national order bars congruent single-sex facilities; facility bans are widespread and one arrest is documented elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private settings are largely outside some bans; some local protections exist; courts have blocked some national orders.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Government buildings, airports, parks and public accommodations are the exposure points; a guardian with a minor may face questioning, and refusal can lead to removal or trespass.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors; national health rules and orders restrict related funding and recognition; no documented visitor emergency-care denial in this record.
care_services.protection: No visitor-specific care protection is documented; national courts have blocked some measures.
care_services.interaction: A visitor's home prescriptions are not directly regulated, but emergency disclosure in a facility could trigger identity questions or access friction.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism and reward language references 'radical gender ideology' and 'radically pro-transgender' groups; state laws mandate pronoun rules and disclosure in schools; official hostility is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; civil-liberties litigation and courts have slowed some measures.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Raises police suspicion and outing risk for visibly transgender or activist travellers; an ordinary tourist is less directly targeted, but the framing colours official encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors, restricts bathroom use in state facilities, and requires school disclosure; national order threatens teachers who support social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: No visitor-specific protection for a transgender minor is documented; national courts have blocked some orders.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces facility exclusion and possible disclosure in government buildings; school rules apply only if enrolled.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated transgender violence incident in this state is recorded; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity; no state anti-discrimination statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; a 2022 poll found 78% support for anti-discrimination covering gender identity; limited local protections exist.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence is uncertain at state level; national recourse exists but is not shown operating for visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unresolved birth-certificate rule, pronoun laws, religious-refusal bill and border policy litigation; no working remedy is documented for facility exclusion or border refusal.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined some national orders; a civil-liberties suit challenges passport policy; national hate-crime law exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Protection is uneven and not operative at the border or in state-run facilities, so the traveller bears the unresolved exposures directly.

anchor_checks.comparison: In 0.35-A an administrative hold ends with an ombudsman securing release and no detention. Here the border can refuse entry and consider permanent fraud ineligibility, and state facility exclusion is operative, so this case is less safe than 0.35-A.

In 0.45-D a hostel refuses a room but a patrol officer declines detention and no criminal warrant exists. Here the exclusion is backed by state facility law and national border screening, with possible trespass escalation, so this case is less safe than 0.45-D.

In 0.65-B a clinic misgenders a visitor but a binding policy is invoked and care proceeds. Here no working remedy is documented for border refusal or government-facility exclusion, so this case is much less safe than 0.65-B.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a hostile national border and document system with state-level facility exclusion and weak local recourse. The border is the harshest unavoidable exposure: a marker or presentation discrepancy can lead to refusal, stranding or a permanent fraud finding, though not automatic. State law permits bathroom exclusion in many government facilities; enforcement is not automatic but can escalate to trespass. Detention and custody carry severe documented harms, but only after arrest or immigration custody. National hate-crime and employment protections and private hospitality reduce everyday risk somewhat, but no working remedy is documented for the traveller-facing border and facility exposures. A lone adult and a guardian with a minor both face outing at these points; the minor adds facility and disclosure risk.
